review_reasons: S1:T1 addresses a decision-changing uncertainty: whether address repair deserves scarce clerk time, rather than assuming the separate O1 timing, O2 surname audit and O3 slip samples are causally linked. Address failure predicts second-location delays with stale entries or household mismatches even outside the O5 burst; the congestion rival predicts delayed accurately addressed pickups concentrated in that interval. Linked second searches with correct addresses and delays tracking congestion would defeat the proposed priority. These observations discriminate contributions, although both causes may coexist and peak-interval marks alone cannot separate queue wait from retrieval duration. The probe uses the existing clerk, behind-desk timing sheet, shelves, cart, paper and pencils and retains identity checks (S1:C1-C3). Its cap includes preparation and correction work (C4), but O6 supplies eight preparation minutes and six subsequent correction minutes; capacity for additional informative recording and its effect on service are unverified. A stop rule prevents an authorized overrun; it does not establish a feasible informative sample. Both probe_feasible and fit therefore remain uncertain despite the source opening labeling its design preserves. The causal proposition is an inference from synthetic stipulations, not a stipulated effect. No unsupported positive benefit needs accepting. Distinct_question is false: the error-linked search signature repeats S1:F01/F02, the accurately located peak-delay rival repeats F04, and the preparation tradeoff repeats F05. Compared with x-fc68a266da383c9e3e4dd966:T1, the simpler marks sample the same address-versus-demand issue; omitting availability-answer timing is not a new question. Four residual tension clusters remain: (1) address failures versus queue congestion as the main delay cause (O1-O3/O5); (2) useful upkeep versus the ten-minute capacity (O6/C4); (3) cart speed versus recency/load/size confounding (O4/F03); and (4) availability certainty versus the representativeness and target relevance of O7 (F06). No unexecuted mark resolves those tensions or establishes 95 percent prompt, correct handoffs.

S1:T1 is relevant because separate S1:O1/O2/O3 counts cannot identify whether address failures explain delayed pickups, and costly upkeep must compete with other uses of the single clerk's time. It predicts stale entries or household-name mismatches in second-location delays, including outside the peak interval; its rival predicts congestion-linked delay despite accurate addresses. Correct entries and surname placement in most second-location delays, with delay instead tracking congestion, defeats address-repair priority. Brief address-error and peak-interval marks on the existing behind-desk timing sheet are a modest diagnostic probe with private names, retained furniture, verified identities and no extra handoff staff. Its timing/error linkage can test association, but unlike the other arm it does not explicitly separate queue wait and retrieval duration, so peak association alone cannot show congestion causes the excess time. Enough informative observations, reliable address-versus-congestion coding, absence of extra service delay and actual preparation headroom remain unconfirmed. S1:O6's eight preparation and six correction minutes do not establish compliance with C4; stopping additional recording at the cap can produce no usable diagnosis. The output's preserves label states design intention, not confirmed compliance or diagnostic feasibility, so both fit and probe_feasible are uncertain. Support is inference from the synthetic observations and S1:F01/F02/F04, not a known causal effect. Distinct_question is false: linked surname/stale-record failures and accurate-address peak delays are already the discriminators in F01/F02/F04, also central to the other arm. Four tensions remain: address versus queue explanations; sufficient diagnosis and upkeep versus clerk preparation/service capacity in O6/C1/C4; cart advantage versus recency/load/size differences in O4/F03; and reported availability burden versus O7 representativeness and the correct, private, prompt-pickup target. The probe does not test cart storage or availability responses, does not price a correction directly, and cannot establish the 95-percent success threshold or a benefit.

S1:T1 makes upkeep priority conditional on a traceable obsolete entry, an avoidable search step and affordable correction time. The upkeep prediction is an unsuccessful search following that entry; the rival is correct initial locations with waiting dominating during O5 demand concentration and availability answers arriving late. Four delayed-encounter traces that show correct initial addresses and queue-dominated time would defeat upkeep priority for that observed batch, not rule out all stale-record effects. Recording waiting separately from search duration is more interpretable than a peak mark alone. Nevertheless, observing and timing one necessary correction is not a controlled estimate of what all corrected pickups would have done; the phrase avoid a demonstrable step remains a counterfactual inference. The next-four-delays bound, ordinary clerk, private notes and unchanged shelves/cart are compatible with S1:C1-C3. Remaining preparation capacity, safe observation of queue wait and retrieval by the sole busy clerk, occurrence of four qualifying encounters, and the ability to time a correction without delaying subsequent readers are unconfirmed (O5/O6/C4). The cap is a guard, not confirmation of informative feasibility, so fit and probe_feasible are uncertain. The proposal explicitly preserves these assumptions and does not establish a benefit from the optional reader question. Distinct_question is false relative to the other arm and the supplied archive: stale-entry search paths repeat S1:F02, household ambiguity repeats F01, queue-versus-retrieval separation repeats F04, correction cost repeats F05, and availability burden repeats F06. Adding answer timestamps and an optional burden question enriches the same diagnostic record; it supplies no independent prediction that an availability intervention, or an interaction between availability and upkeep, would outperform the archived explanations. Four residual clusters remain: (1) error-caused searching versus congestion (O1-O3/O5); (2) upkeep cost versus C4 capacity (O6); (3) cart performance versus recency/load/size (O4/F03); and (4) availability burden versus interview representativeness and the prompt-correct-pickup target (O7/F06). The source itself retains the cart uncertainty; its trace does not resolve it. Support is inference throughout, with no measured outcome or stakeholder agreement.

S1:T1 connects location-upkeep priority to two observable requirements: obsolete entries actually precede second searches, and a needed correction has affordable cost under S1:C4. It also preserves availability uncertainty as a potentially independent burden from S1:O7. Its location-bottleneck prediction is an obsolete entry followed by a wasted search step; its rival predicts correct initial locations, peak-window waiting and late verified availability answers. Correct first locations throughout the traced delayed batch with waiting dominating retrieval defeats upkeep priority for that batch. Tracing four delayed encounters, queue wait, first/actual locations, name errors, second-search duration and availability-answer timing can reveal these different signatures. Optional post-handoff burden questions and one timed necessary correction use existing paper/timing resources behind the desk with clerk-only handoffs. However, four delayed encounters may not occur, selecting only delayed encounters cannot estimate whether errors disproportionately cause delays across ordinary pickups, and a one-clerk trace/question can slow subsequent service. O6/C4 supply no confirmed remaining correction/recording capacity, so both probe_feasible and fit remain uncertain despite the explicit cap. Correcting an entry has not been shown to avoid a future search; the trace identifies a plausible wasted step rather than demonstrating intervention efficacy. The cause hypothesis is inferential. Distinct_question is false: the obsolete-entry search path is S1:F02, the accurate-location queue rival is F04, corrective work consuming clerk capacity is F05, and separate perceived availability burden is F06. Integrating their time fields and measuring one correction sharpens selection evidence but adds no established new causal path or discriminator beyond the archive. Four tensions remain: location versus congestion priority in O1/O3/O5; correction and diagnostic effort versus O6/C4 capacity; availability-answer timing/perceived burden versus O7 representativeness and the objective correct-pickup target; and the cart interpretation under O4/F03. The optional question and four-case trace cannot resolve the latter two or establish a 95-percent outcome.

contrast_reviews: Both S1:T1 openings test essentially the same address-error versus congestion explanation already represented by S1:F01/F02/F04. x-fc68a266da383c9e3e4dd966 uses a next-four-delays event trace with explicit queue duration, verified-availability timing and one correction cost, whereas x-4a4a9504e34e2cf662b3f50e uses lighter ordinary-pickup address and peak marks. The richer trace can make delay attribution more interpretable; selecting only delays also limits rate estimation and unbiased comparison with prompt pickups. Neither supplies a new causal question beyond the archive, and neither establishes adequate clerk capacity. Their source fit labels differ, but the unconfirmed recording and correction capacity warrants uncertain findings for both. The longer account earns no novelty or operational-benefit credit.

Both S1:T1 openings prioritize linking existing address and congestion explanations before choosing an intervention, and both substantially reuse S1:F01/F02/F04/F05. x-fc68a266da383c9e3e4dd966 adds a four-delayed-encounter event trace, explicit queue/retrieval decomposition, availability-answer timing, an optional burden question and one correction-cost measurement. x-4a4a9504e34e2cf662b3f50e proposes briefer routine address/peak marks and wrong-reader monitoring. The detailed trace can better partition a witnessed delay and price one correction, but delayed-only selection does not supply a general causal comparison or prove that updating records prevents future delay. The briefer probe may have lower recording burden but weaker queue discrimination. These measurement and burden differences do not establish archive-distinct causal questions; both retain unverified capacity and unresolved availability/cart concerns.

review_reasons: S1:T1 would change whether location upkeep merits priority over demand or storage explanations. Its address-error prediction links stale entries or household-name mismatches to delayed encounters beyond the O5 busy interval; its rival predicts waiting-driven delay even when locations are accurate. A linked sample in which address failures rarely explain excess search time and waiting explains accurate-location delays would defeat that priority. Separating waiting from retrieval and noting arrival recency/cart load helps avoid inferring cause from O1-O4 aggregate counts. There is no executed comparison, and simultaneous address error and congestion remain possible. Existing paper, timing sheet, clerk, private storage and identity checks respect the intended C1-C3 scope; stopping optional recording when daily preparation or upkeep cannot remain within C4 guards compliance. It does not establish enough variation or recording capacity: O6 gives an eight-minute preparation day plus six correction minutes, and the only clerk may be unable to observe queue and search durations without changing service. Fit and probe_feasible are uncertain, consistent with the opening. Support is inference: address and queue hypotheses follow synthetic observations and archive relations; intervention efficacy is not established. Distinct_question is false. S1:F01/F02 already require encounter-level error linkage, F04 already distinguishes waiting from actual retrieval, F03 already requires comparable cart loads, and F05 already identifies displaced correction work. The added columns operationalize these archived relations. Relative to x-3a95fbb89d38f35764f57115:T1/T2, this arm remains passive diagnosis rather than proposing a different causal test. Four unresolved clusters remain: (1) location errors versus demand as the principal bottleneck (O1-O3/O5); (2) informative diagnosis and upkeep versus preparation/service capacity (O6/C4); (3) cart speed versus recency, load and size confounds (O4/F03, with size not controlled here); and (4) availability certainty versus representative reader burden and success-target relevance (O7/F06). No additional stock, staffing or proven reader effect is warranted.

S1:T1 targets a decision-changing gap: the timing, surname audit and exception-slip samples in S1:O1/O2/O3 are unlinked, so location upkeep cannot yet be prioritized over congestion or availability responses. It predicts stale entries or household-name mismatches in delayed encounters, including outside the burst; the rival predicts delays chiefly from waiting even with accurate locations during S1:O5's concentrated interval. Rare address-error contributions with waiting dominating accurate-location delays defeats prioritizing location uncertainty. Splitting queue wait from retrieval time, recording second-search reasons and location accuracy, and adding arrival recency/cart-load observations is a useful bounded diagnostic design. Existing sheets, paper, shelves/cart and the single clerk supply the nominal resources; private notes and verified handoffs preserve the intended S1:C1-C3 rules. Nevertheless, simultaneous notes and handoffs may themselves slow service, enough variation and reliable cause coding are unconfirmed, and the O6 eight-minute preparation plus six-minute correction record does not demonstrate headroom under the ten-minute C4 allowance. A stop rule bounds effort but can leave inadequate evidence. Actual probe_feasible and fit are uncertain. Its causal claims are plausible inferences, not stipulated causes or measured effects. Distinct_question is false: S1:F01/F02 already give the linked name/stale-location delay signatures, F04 already predicts waiting for correctly located books during bursts, and F03 already preserves recency/load confounding. It combines those archive discriminators and differs from the other arm's active update comparison, but does not establish a new causal question relative to the archive. Four tensions remain: location errors versus queue causes; informative diagnosis/upkeep versus O6/C4 capacity and possible observation-induced delay; cart benefit versus O4/O5 selection; and availability certainty/O7 representativeness versus correct, private, two-minute pickup. No intervention, availability benefit or 95-percent result is established.

S1:T1 asks a decision-relevant counterfactual: for comparable displaced holds, does keeping the private exception slip current at moves improve retrieval beyond giving an availability-only answer? Updates predict fewer second searches and shorter pickup time; the rival predicts comparable uncertainty relief from the answer while updates add work and leave queue or household-name delays intact. Updates that consume preparation capacity without reducing second searches or pickup duration defeat their priority in the proposed rehearsal. S1:T2 separately predicts a residual cart advantage with equally current records and matched recency, size and load, versus disappearance of the O4 advantage; no faster matched cart searches, or inability to hold equivalent loads, defeats that storage claim. T2 is only an optional subsequent rehearsal, not an executed result. Both use existing clerk, paper, shelves/cart and private records with identity checks (C1-C3); preparation and restoration count toward C4. Whether T1 fits the remaining allowance is indispensable and unknown given O6, and T2 additionally requires spare cart capacity and preparation time. Rehearsing the same holds invites learning of their locations even with alternating order; its resemblance to live queue conditions is also unverified. Probe_feasible and fit are uncertain for both openings and hence this arm. Support is inference for the proposed mechanisms. The assertion that verified answers reduce reported uncertainty in both conditions is a hypothetical prediction motivated by O7, not an observed causal effect; the text correctly requires a later reader comparison to assess it, and the current rehearsal cannot support that benefit. Distinct_question is true only for T1: unlike the other arm's association record and the separate S1:F02/F05/F06 signatures, it manipulates move-triggered location updates against an availability-answer comparator and asks whether the additional physical-search benefit justifies measured upkeep cost. This is a distinct discriminating intervention question, not a new assertion that stale records cause searching. T2 is archive-equivalent to S1:F03, and its optional presence contributes no separate novelty. Four residual clusters remain: (1) stale records versus household error/congestion as the delay source (O1-O3/O5); (2) upkeep/rehearsal cost versus C4 (O6); (3) cart speed versus comparability/capacity (O4/T2/F03); and (4) availability effects and reader representativeness versus the actual prompt, private, correct-handoff target (O7/F06).

S1:T1 and S1:T2 are both assessed. T1 makes a decision-relevant intervention comparison: availability answers alone versus updating the private exception slip when a book moves. For comparable displaced holds, it predicts fewer second searches and shorter pickups with updates; its rival predicts equal uncertainty relief from answers but no retrieval advantage because household-name failures or queues dominate. Spending the preparation allowance without improving second searches or duration defeats T1. Alternated same-hold rehearsals, identity-error records and preparation timing use existing paper and the timing sheet, but repeated searches can introduce memory effects and cannot reproduce arrival queues or measure reader uncertainty. The claim of greater availability certainty with updates outruns its prediction of uncertainty reduction in both conditions; the proposal correctly defers reader effects to a later comparison, leaving this differential speculative. T2 separately asks whether cart speed survives matching recency, size and search load with equally current locations. Persistent speed versus disappearance after matching are different predictions; no speed advantage or inadequate equivalent cart capacity defeats T2. Its optional cart/shelf rehearsals include restoration time but rely on unconfirmed cart capacity and residual clerk time. S1:O6 supplies eight preparation minutes and six correction minutes, not verified headroom under S1:C4; neither the cap nor a conditional start proves either rehearsal is feasible. Privacy, clerk-only handoffs and existing furniture are intended to preserve S1:C1-C3, with no proposed relaxation. Both probe_feasible and fit are uncertain. Distinct_question is true specifically for T1: unlike the other arm's cause-observation probe, it specifies a move-triggered corrective operation and an answer-only comparator to test its marginal retrieval benefit against measured upkeep cost. S1:F02/F05/F06 contain its causal ingredients but do not supply this intervention contrast or its same-hold counterfactual discriminator. T2 is equivalent to the matched-load question in S1:F03 and adds no novelty. Four tensions remain: stale records versus household names/queue causes of delays in S1:O1/O2/O3/O5; upkeep/rehearsal effort versus C4 and O6; the unsupported differential certainty claim and unrepresentative O7 burden evidence versus the objective pickup target; and cart speed versus recency/load/size selection in O4/F03. No rehearsal, reader comparison or benefit has occurred.

contrast_reviews: x-6ee2a48c0163940835f083f1:T1 observes encounter-level location accuracy, waiting and storage covariates. x-3a95fbb89d38f35764f57115:T1 instead compares move-triggered record updating with availability-only answering on the same displaced holds, adding a counterfactual retrieval-and-upkeep-cost question; its rehearsal cannot test reported reader uncertainty or ordinary congestion. That limited distinction supports distinct_question for the second arm, not an intervention-benefit claim. Its T2 matched cart-versus-shelf rehearsal repeats S1:F03 and remains parked unless capacity exists. Both retain uncertain preparation fit and all four unresolved tension clusters. Differences in number of openings and detail alone carry no credit.

x-3a95fbb89d38f35764f57115:S1:T1 manipulates a specific maintenance trigger and compares updated locations against availability-only answers, asking whether marginal retrieval benefit earns its clerk-time cost. That intervention contrast is locally distinct from the supplied archive's observational signatures, although it uses archived causal ingredients and its claimed differential certainty benefit remains speculative and unmeasured. Its S1:T2 cart comparison repeats S1:F03. x-6ee2a48c0163940835f083f1:S1:T1 instead links routine errors, waiting and retrieval to distinguish archived address and congestion explanations before intervening. The active rehearsal versus diagnostic observation difference matters to what can be learned, but neither establishes real reader benefit or verified preparation capacity. review_reasons: S2:T1 can change whether material-access redesign merits attention: with identical pattern counts and equivalent checking, adjacent allotments predict fewer crossed reaches and picking omissions; the pattern-mixture/checking rival predicts disappearance of the omission advantage despite fewer reaches. Equal or worse picking errors, or errors arising mainly in filling, defeats the proposed picking mechanism for the compared batches. Recording setup, replenishment, assembly and checking also avoids treating O1's 86 minutes as total readiness time; its additional eleven-minute check gives a stipulated 97-minute sequence, not a tested effect of a new layout. The two twelve-kit blocks use existing supplies, exactly two volunteers and the existing table, and stop rules preserve the intent of C1-C4. However, adjacent supplies fitting alongside opened stock is explicitly unconfirmed, stock sufficiency is not guaranteed by O5, and collecting stage-error and reach tallies while both volunteers assemble may change their workload. The first comparison has shared and adjacent layouts in one order; reversal only in a later replication does not remove current learning or fatigue confounding. Neither an informative 24-kit comparison inside 90 minutes nor sixty-kit completion is established. Thus probe_feasible and fit are uncertain rather than accepting the opening's preserves label. Support is inference from O2-O4 and the supplied concerns. Common pencil markings are feasible candidate safeguards with untested distribution benefit, and no added observer or production gain is assumed. Distinct_question is true specifically for its proposed picking-versus-filling error localization. S2:F02/F03 already contain the main access/reach and matched-layout relation; F01 merely lists filling losses as an alternative, without an expected stage-transition observation. Recording which stage first loses an item asks a further observational question relative to those archive signatures and to x-36d50e2f91779cfd71206421:T1, whose audit is before correction but not specified before and after filling. This distinction is limited by the absence of a detailed stage-observation method; it is not a new shared-access mechanism. Five unresolved clusters remain: (1) access causation versus pattern/check/order confounds (O3/O4/F03); (2) picking versus filling origin (O2/unknowns); (3) stock continuity and staging footprint versus C3/C4 (O5); (4) bounded-probe timing versus the sixty-kit deadline and checking tail (O1/C2/F05); and (5) complete contents versus correct exterior pattern identity and untested markings (O7/F06).

S2:T1 asks whether adjacent allotments reduce picking omissions under matched patterns and checks, rather than attributing S2:O4 to access without controlling its easier-mixture/unequal-checking rival. This is relevant to complete, prompt kits under S2:O1/O2 and C1/C2. It predicts fewer picking omissions and crossed reaches; equal or more picking omissions despite reduced reaching, or mainly filling-stage losses, defeats that explanation. Recording picking versus filling errors, replenishment and all setup, assembly and checking time adds useful diagnostic detail. Two twelve-kit batches use twenty-four kits and existing resources, with stopping rules for time and table fit. Actual stock, enough kits of each pattern, simultaneous opened-supply footprint and observation/correction costs remain unknown, so probe_feasible and fit are uncertain despite the opening's preserves label. This first ordered comparison leaves learning, fatigue and order confounded with layout; reversing order only in an unspecified later replication does not repair the scored probe or guarantee a later probe fits. The before/after error-stage distinction refines the same S2:F02-F03 access comparison, and filling losses are already a rival preserved in S2:F01; neither a larger batch nor additional recording establishes distinct_question relative to the supplied archive. Four tensions remain: access versus pattern/checking and failure-stage causes; layout versus learning/fatigue in the ordered batches; twenty-four-kit diagnostic effort versus stock, footprint and sixty-kit readiness under S2:O1/O5/C2/C3; and complete contents versus exterior identity/distribution in S2:O2/O7/F06. The arithmetic 86 plus 11 equals 97 follows S2:O1, but S2:F05 preserves uncertainty about checking details and the separate audit; it supplies no tested intervention result. Pencilled pattern marks remain an untested common addition.

S2:T1 tests whether the apparent loose-material advantage in O4 survives pattern matching, equivalent audits and comparable volunteer exposure. The access hypothesis predicts fewer reaches and pre-correction missing items without increased full setup/assembly/check time; the rival predicts that matching mixture and audit exposure removes the advantage even if reaches fall. Unchanged or higher omissions with fewer reaches, or setup/checking erasing the time gain, defeats the proposed advantage for this small comparison. A tie is explicitly inconclusive and twelve kits cannot establish rare-error rates or sixty-kit delivery. Each volunteer making one kit of each pattern per layout in opposite orders improves control of volunteer and order differences over a single sequential block comparison, although learning can still carry between conditions. Production-kit use, exactly two volunteers, existing supplies, preserved specified contents, a fit check and a ninety-minute cap respect the intended C1-C4 design. Actual table footprint, enough required kits of each pattern for the match, usable stock and capacity for audits and corrections within remaining production time are unconfirmed (O1/O5/unknowns). A refusal to start a layout that cannot fit guards the boundary but does not confirm a workable probe; both probe_feasible and fit remain uncertain despite the preserves label. Support is inference from authored O2-O4; no reduction in volunteer burden or distribution errors is established. Pencilling patterns is a common safeguard held constant, not evidence of an identity effect. Distinct_question is false: the principal mechanism and matched comparator repeat S2:F02/F03. Counterbalancing volunteers/order and shrinking the batch improve the design of the same discriminator; they do not add a different causal or observational question. Relative to x-7df569e962f9d82b6b940e44:T1, this opening does not localize losses by separately recording picking and filling; auditing missing items before correction can still observe errors arising at either stage. Five remaining clusters are (1) access versus mixture/check/learning attribution (O3/O4/F03); (2) picking versus filling origin (O2/unknowns); (3) available stock and table footprint (O5/C3/C4); (4) diagnostic time and check tail versus all-sixty readiness within C2 (O1/F05); and (5) completeness versus correct distribution identity and untested markings (O7/F06). They are retained uncertainties, not resolved effects.

S2:T1 links personal staging to reduced reaching and pre-correction missing items, while explicitly challenging whether S2:O4 was comparable to S2:O1/O2. An observed advantage under matched patterns and identical audits would affect the choice to investigate material access; loss of the advantage after matching supports its mixture/checking rival. Fewer reaches with unchanged or increased omissions, an erased total-time advantage, or inability to fit defeats the proposal. Each volunteer performing one kit of each pattern under each layout, with opposite orders, produces a bounded twelve-kit comparison using the supplied two volunteers, table and materials. Existing pencil pattern marks are held common and their distribution benefit is expressly untested. However, sufficient assigned kits of each pattern, stock continuity, opened-supply footprint, and the cost of preparation, tallying, auditing and corrections within the overall 90 minutes are unverified. Its stated preserves classification confuses guarded intention with confirmed resource fit; both feasibility and fit are uncertain under S2:C1-C4. Pre-correction omission counts do not independently locate loss at picking versus filling. S2:F02-F03 already state the reaching/access causal path and matched-comparison discriminator, with S2:F01 preserving alternative filling losses; T1 is useful but distinct_question is false relative to the archive and the other arm's access comparison. Three remaining tensions are access-linked errors versus mixture/checking and picking/filling explanations; the small probe versus full-run stock, table and checked completion under S2:O1/O5/C2/C3; and assembly completeness versus externally clear pattern assignment at distribution under S2:O2/O7/F06. All support is inferential from synthetic stipulations, with no tested reduction in burden or errors.

contrast_reviews: Both S2:T1 openings repeat the archive's shared-access versus mixture/checking comparison. x-36d50e2f91779cfd71206421 improves its design with opposite volunteer orders and twelve production kits; x-7df569e962f9d82b6b940e44 uses two twelve-kit blocks and would reverse order only in a later replication. Those sample and order differences do not constitute new questions. The substantive added observational distinction in x-7df569e962f9d82b6b940e44 is recording picking versus filling errors: an item absent when picked differs from one correctly picked but subsequently lost in filling, and the latter would redirect attention away from picking access. That opening does not specify the observation protocol as clearly as a pre/post filling audit, so its feasibility remains uncertain. Both leave stock, space, deadline and distribution tensions unresolved; neither produces a tested full-session benefit.

The core S2:T1 predictions in both arms are equivalent to S2:F02-F03: matched local access should reduce omissions, while matching may remove the small-batch advantage. x-36d50e2f91779cfd71206421 balances volunteer/layout order in twelve production kits; x-7df569e962f9d82b6b940e44 uses two ordered twelve-kit batches and records picking versus filling losses and replenishment. Stage recording can expose a filling-loss alternative, while the larger ordered probe adds resource burden and leaves an additional order explanation. These are real differences in measurement and confounding control, not evidence that either arm has found a new causal question beyond the supplied archive. Neither proposal demonstrates deadline, table, stock or distribution success.

review_reasons: S2:T1 addresses whether local material access merits redesign after O4's uncontrolled small-batch result. Matched patterns and checks predict fewer crossed reaches and omissions with no greater checked-kit time under local access; the rival predicts removal of the omission/time advantage after matching mixture and checking, even if reaches decrease. Equal or worse omissions or checked-kit time, or a layout that cannot fit, defeats its proposed advantage in that bounded comparison. Merely seeing fewer reaches would not validate an omission mechanism, and a small zero-error tie supplies little discriminatory information. The two matched six-kit blocks, reversal across volunteers, stock count and layout measurement use the supplied resources and anticipate C1-C4. All setup and checking enter the same ninety-minute budget. Required usable stock, matching the actual pattern assignment, combined supply footprint, and performing tallying/auditing with exactly two assemblers are nevertheless unconfirmed; the probe may stop without an informative comparison. Fit and probe_feasible remain uncertain, agreeing with the source opening rather than treating its guarded intent as established feasibility. Inference is the appropriate support level: O2/O3/O4 motivate the mechanism, but neither effect nor stock sufficiency is stipulated. Pencilled envelope patterns are held constant and their distribution benefit remains untested. Distinct_question is false. The matched-access relation and confound rival repeat S2:F02/F03, and checking quantities before closing observes a final kit without specifying separate picked-content and post-filling observations. Compared with x-a4633aae6a5ab649bfb900bc:T1, it therefore does not add the stage-localization discriminator. Stock/space verification and a smaller matched sample improve procedural boundaries of an existing question. Five residual clusters remain: (1) access cause versus mixture/check/learning effects (O3/O4/F03); (2) picking versus filling as error origin (O2/unknowns); (3) usable reserve stock and layout footprint versus C3/C4 (O5); (4) twelve-kit diagnostic time versus all-sixty readiness and end-check cost (O1/C2/F05); and (5) complete contents versus identifiable assigned patterns and untested markings (O7/F06). The opening explicitly disclaims extrapolation, so no physical, operational or agreement claim follows.

S2:T1 addresses the decision-changing ambiguity between shared-access errors suggested by S2:O2/O3/O4 and an easier pattern mixture or unequal checking in the small batch. It predicts fewer reaches and omissions, without worse checked-kit time, under matched local access; the rival predicts no omission or timing advantage after matching even if reaching decreases. Equal or worse omissions or checked-kit time defeats the stated advantage, and a layout that cannot fit defeats feasibility. Stock counting and layout measurement are appropriate prerequisite checks, and two matched six-kit blocks with volunteer order reversal, common pattern marks and equivalent quantity/dimension checks use existing resources. They remain unexecuted: sufficient stock and pattern assignments, occupied table area, and the timing cost of setup, observation and correction are unknown under S2:C1-C4. The single 90-minute cap bounds an attempted probe but does not show that the comparison and remaining production fit; uncertain is appropriate for both probe_feasible and fit. Checking only before closing, without independently recording picked contents first, does not by itself distinguish picking from filling loss; this limits its claimed mechanism discrimination. The proposed markings' effect on S2:O7 is untested, not an established safeguard outcome. T1 repeats S2:F02-F03's access versus comparable-mixture question and shares that causal test with the other arm, so distinct_question is false. Three unresolved tensions are causal access effects versus mixture/checking or failure-stage explanations; bounded comparison versus sixty-kit time, restocking and table requirements in S2:O1/O5/C2/C3; and contents reliability versus exterior pattern identity and distribution accuracy in S2:O2/O7. The synthetic facts support a plausible inference, not a successful intervention.

S2:T1 would change attention between picking access and envelope filling: it proposes comparing picked contents before filling with contents after filling, in addition to the common matched-layout comparison. Loose access predicts fewer picking omissions and crossed reaches without increased fully audited time; the rival predicts no matched access advantage, with losses persisting during filling despite fewer reaches. An initially correct picked set that becomes incomplete in the envelope is a different observation from an already incomplete picked set.
